newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto urges action on Indonesia poll violations.
newsitem.headline: Suharto urges action on Indonesia poll violations.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto has ordered the government's election organisers to reprimand the three approved political parties for increasing campaign violations, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Amid continuing large street parades and motor processions in violation of election rules, Suharto said the parties were obliged to control their supporters.
"Don't continue violating the election rules," Interior Minister Yogie Memet, who is also General Election Institute (LPU) chairman, quoted Suharto as saying during a meeting on Tuesday.

Fearing outbreaks of street violence, the government this year banned street parades and processions during the 27-day election campaign which began on April 27. The nation's 125 million electors are due to cast their vote on May 29.

The government also tightened restrictions on the television and radio broadcast of party speeches to the nation of more than 200 million people, requiring all material to be cleared through a government censor.

The Jakarta Post said Memet, together with Attorney-General Singgih who chairs the official election supervision committee, had told Suharto that campaign-related traffic accidents had claimed 49 lives and injured hundreds in the first 16 days of the campaign.
Singgih quoted Suharto as saying the leaders of the parties must be held responsible for order and security during rallies.

He said Suharto had also ordered him to enforce the new regulations created this week which prohibited banners and pictures potraying an alliance between the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
"We ask the three contestants' task forces to haul down those banners and pictures," Singgih said, adding banners and other campaign material must be approved by the police.

Only the government-backed faction of the PDI led by Surjadi, the PPP and the ruling Golkar are allowed to contest the poll. The LPU last year rejected a list of election candidates put forward by Megawati, saying she did not represent the genuine wing of the PDI.
PPP Secretary-General Tosari Wijaya was quoted by the Jakarta Post as saying the party could not stop people from making banners linking Megawati with his party.
"It's not appropriate to ban people from expressing their political aspirations," Wijaya told reporters.
"We cannot stop those supporters participating in the campaign. Everything has been spontaneous."
PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying the appearance of the slogan "Mega-Bintang" had nothing to do with Megawati.
"Mega-Bintang means great star. It has nothing to do with Megawati," Metareum told reporters.
But people waving the banners have said it represents the alliance between supporters of Megawati and the PPP, which uses the star, or bintang, as its symbol.
